name: Budae Jjigae (Korean Army Base Stew)
why: A bubbling one-pot Korean hot pot born from American-Korean fusion — Spam, sausages, kimchi, mushrooms and ramen simmered in a gochujang broth, finished with cheese. The ultimate cold-October comfort bowl, and a fun deep-dive into Korean hot pot culture.
author: Henry
ingredients: 4 cocktail Frankfurt sausages (150g), thinly & diagonally sliced
200g enoki mushrooms, base stem removed & separated
200g king oyster mushrooms, thinly sliced lengthways
1/2 cup aged kimchi, cut into bite-sized pieces
50g Korean rice cakes for soup (soak frozen ones in cold water 15 mins)
Sauce: few sprinkles ground black pepper

steps: Whisk the sauce ingredients (gochugaru, mirin, soy sauce, minced garlic, sugar, gochujang and black pepper) together in a small bowl until the paste breaks down.
Thinly slice the Spam and cut the sausages thinly on the diagonal. Slice the tofu into 1.5cm-thick slabs.
Separate the enoki from the base, slice the king oyster lengthways and the shiitake caps thinly. Cut the kimchi into bite-sized pieces and slice the green onion.
If using frozen rice cakes, soak them in cold water for 15 minutes until softened.
Assemble everything in a shallow wide pot (except the ramen, rice cakes, green onion and cheese). Spoon the sauce into the middle and pour the chicken stock around the edge.
Cover and bring to the boil over medium-high heat, simmering until the stock is bubbling and the kimchi starts to release its juices (about 8 minutes).
Top with the ramen noodles, rice cakes, green onion and cheese. Boil uncovered until the ramen is just cooked and the cheese is melted (2-3 minutes) — don't overcook the noodles or they turn to mush.
If you're eating at the table, drop the heat to low so it keeps bubbling gently through the meal.
Ladle the broth, meat, mushrooms and noodles into bowls.
Serve with steamed white rice and a side of extra kimchi or any Korean banchan on hand.

pro_tips: Aged kimchi (6+ months) gives the deeper, sharper sourness that defines authentic budae jjigae — its brine adds acidity that fresh kimchi can't.
This is a communal hot pot: keep it on the stove at the table and top up with a second block of ramen and more cheese as the pot empties. That's the whole ritual.
